title: needs-decision: is a documented single-target fast path worth adding to issue-authoring's Stage 2 release protocol?
body:
## Background

`skills/issue-authoring/references/workflow-boundary.md`'s Stage 2
release protocol requires the same number of sequential marker
round-trips (heartbeat -> release -> release-guard -> release-complete,
each with its own re-fetch/verify and settle-delay wait) for a
single-target standalone orphan set as for an N-target roadmap release,
even though a lone target with no anchor/child distinction has no
split-ownership risk to guard against. A field-feedback gist raised this
as a process/ergonomics observation, explicitly flagged as "not a bug --
the protocol is safe as specified" and "optional to file." Verified
2026-09-14: no existing issue (open or closed) already covers this
specific ceremony-reduction idea.

## Proposed change

This is a maintainer judgment call on whether the added protocol-surface
complexity of a documented fast path is worth the ceremony reduction, not
a correctness fix:

- **A -- leave as-is.** The current uniform protocol is simple to reason
  about and already proven safe; do not add a second, narrower code path
  for the single-target case.
- **B -- add a documented single-target fast path.** For a lone orphan
  target with no anchor/child split-ownership risk (i.e. `target` equals
  `anchor` throughout its own marker log), collapse some of the
  heartbeat/release/release-guard/release-complete round-trips, since
  there is no other target whose state could have drifted in between.
- **C -- partial simplification.** Keep the full state-machine shape but
  relax only the settle-delay wait durations for the single-target case,
  without removing any marker step outright.

## Acceptance criteria

- A maintainer decision is recorded on this issue (e.g. `Maintainer decision (Groom hearing, <date>): <resolution>`) selecting one of the options above or a variant.
- If a protocol change is chosen, a follow-up implementation issue captures the concrete wording change to `workflow-boundary.md` and its own acceptance criteria.

Refs #2993

## Groom decision

Maintainer decision (Groom hearing, 2026-09-15): choose option A and leave the uniform Stage 2 release protocol as-is. Its consistent fail-closed state machine is worth the additional round-trips, so a single-target fast path is not planned. Close this issue as not planned.

## Notes

The previous authoring generation was already completed under roadmap #2993; its append-only owner and publication-intent history remains on the roadmap record.
